context: Add a small helper (scripts/set_worktree_identity.sh) invoked by worktree-claim after the worktree exists. It must: (1) refuse and exit non-zero when the resolved GLOBAL identity is itself a known agent/service identity, rather than propagating it; (2) require extensions.worktreeConfig=true, enabling it on the common repo if absent; (3) write ONLY via `git config --worktree` inside the claimed worktree; (4) be idempotent, so re-claiming is a no-op; (5) leave the ephemeral-clone path (no pool) untouched, since a plain clone has no linked worktree and --worktree is meaningless there. Document the behavior in one concise AGENTS.md line under the worktree section. Land after shared-clone-git-identity-drift-guard-v3 so the audit warning channel and the AGENTS.md edits do not collide.
description: Set a --worktree-scoped human Git identity on every pool worktree at claim time, so a stray write to the shared common config becomes inert instead of reauthoring every worktree at once. This is the prevention half that shared-clone-git-identity-drift-v2/-guard-v3 explicitly declined to attempt ('detection and instruction hardening, not prevention: do not claim that the audit can stop another live session from writing .git/config'). That premise is refuted by config precedence, measured directly. MECHANISM (verified in a scratch repo, not inferred): running `git config user.email X` with no --global from INSIDE a linked worktree writes to the COMMON config, i.e. the primary clone's .git/config. Reproduction: init primary, `git worktree add ../pool-09`, then from pool-09 run `git config user.email noreply@anthropic.com` -- primary/.git/config gains that [user] block although it never ran the command, and every other worktree inherits it. That single write explains all the Claude-authored stashes across four different pool worktrees; they do not require four separate write events. FIX, also measured: with extensions.worktreeConfig=true (already enabled on the maintainer's clone) and `git config --worktree user.email joeharris76@gmail.com` set in the worktree, re-contaminating the common config leaves the worktree resolving `Joe Harris <joeharris76@gmail.com>` from .git/worktrees/<name>/config.worktree. A third measurement shows a sibling worktree WITHOUT the override still resolves the agent identity, so the override must be applied per worktree -- which makes `make worktree-claim` the only correct hook point. Cleanup of stale instruction text cannot substitute for this: the instruction's source is an external agent harness still in service, so the supply does not stop.

anti_patterns.dont: Delete or rewrite the Claude-authored stashes, or amend/rebase existing commits, while doing this work
anti_patterns.instead: Leave them untouched; forensics is tracked separately
anti_patterns.why: They are the forensic record of the writer, and a prior identity-history rewrite in this repo corrupted 2286 commits on main undetected for ~2.5 months

anti_patterns.dont: Set or propagate an agent/service identity anywhere to make a check pass
anti_patterns.instead: Exit non-zero with the resolved identity and its config origins, and require the human identity be fixed first
anti_patterns.why: [COMMIT-IDENTITY-001] rejects agent identities as author, and a green check bought that way hides the exact condition being guarded

anti_patterns.dont: Treat a detection warning as sufficient and close this without the precedence change
anti_patterns.instead: Land the --worktree override, whose effectiveness is measured, and keep detection as the backstop
anti_patterns.why: shared-clone-git-identity-drift-v2/-guard-v3 both scoped themselves to detection, and the contamination recurred anyway across four worktrees

anti_patterns.dont: Write user.name/user.email into the shared common .git/config to normalize identity
anti_patterns.instead: Write only with `git config --worktree` inside the claimed worktree, so precedence overrides whatever the common config holds
anti_patterns.why: That write IS the defect under repair: from any linked worktree it lands in the primary clone's config and reauthors every pool worktree at once

preserves.behavior: The ephemeral-clone path (BENCHBOX_EPHEMERAL_CLONE=1, no pool present) is unaffected and still requires no worktree identity
The primary clone's own config is never written by this change
make agent-write-preflight keeps refusing an agent author identity; this item adds prevention, it does not relax the existing gate
make worktree-claim continues to claim and print the binding work order exactly as it does today

verifications.expected: worktree resolves the human identity from config.worktree while the common config holds an agent identity
